Sources: raw arXiv HTML (Tables 2-5, Sec 6-7 text), the Fig. 3 PNG, and the authors' artifact files fetched verbatim from raw.githubusercontent.com: paper_results_figure2.csv, repro_figure2.sh, repro_table4.sh, README.md. Batch 1: 'Unless otherwise stated, across all our experiments, batch size is 1 and llama.cpp is made to use as many CPU threads as physical cores (i.e., 16 on cli1 and cli3, 8 on cli2)'. The -ngl baseline is confirmed as whole-layer offload: 'For our baselines, we performed this search process for each model-budget combination to find the maximal number of layers that fit within the given VRAM budget'. The artifact runs '"$LLAMA_CLI" -m "$gguf_path" -c "$ctx_tokens" --file "$ctx_file" --temp 0.0 -no-cnv -n "$GEN_TOKENS" --no-display-prompt -ub "$ub" -ngl "$ngl" $THREAD_ARGS', with no -cmoe/-ot. VRAM budget definition: pipelined sharding gets '-mva N | Max VRAM allocation budget in MB' (README) covering all GPU-resident state; the paper says 'our VRAM budget specification is always in multiples of 1,000 MB', but both artifact scripts use 'VRAM_BUDGETS_MB=(2048 4096 6144 8192 12288 ...)' (1,024-MB multiples), so '2G' is 2.15 GB in the artifact. Derived -ngl baseline tok/s mix two runs: Table 4 TPS comes from repro_table4.sh ('GEN_TOKENS=256', 'UBATCH=1024'), while the Fig. 2 speedups come from repro_figure2.sh ('GEN_TOKENS=100', best of ub 1024/2048 per README: 'each bar in Figure 2 represents the best speedup across ubatch sizes (1024, 2048)'). The derivation is approximate at the few-% level. Host: Table 3 'cli3 | 5090 | 32 | 16 (EPYC) | 256 | 153.6 | 50 (64 theoretical peak value)'. Mem BW is stated; the CPU model is not. PCIe Gen5 is confirmed by Sec 7: 'from gen5 (64 GBps) to gen3 (16 GBps)'. Output length is ambiguous: the paper says 'We measure TPS over 100+ output tokens' and the Table 4 script generates 256, so ctx is 1024 + 50..128. Checked: Table 4 qwen30b 1K 2G TPS = 25.7 (row 'qwen- | 1K | 25.7 | 26.2 | 29.6 | 32.1 | 36.5 | 47.8 | 158.1 | 158.6'). CSV 'qwen3-30b,1K,2G,2.84,1.33,1.53' gives 25.7/1.33 = 19.32. The artifact NGL lookup 'qwen3-30b,1024,2048,1024=3' gives -ngl 3. -CMOE TIE: in Fig. 3 ('TTFT and TPS speedups from pipelined sharding vs llama.cpp's manual CPU offloading'), the 1K/2G 'TPS Speedup (MoE only)' bar top measured by pixel sits at 0.99x (gridlines 0 at y=545.5 and 1 at y=473.5; bar top at y=474.5). The -cmoe baseline is therefore ~26.0 tok/s and not distinct from the system's 25.7 within figure precision. This is a real tie, not an extraction error, and the text agrees: 'Manual offloading can match our automatic approach's TPS at low VRAM budgets and small contexts'. The -cmoe baseline is 'applied atop llama-cpp-baseline' (i.e., the -ngl found for the budget, plus -cmoe), so it probably uses well under the 2G budget. equal_vram=true means 'within the same budget', not 'same VRAM used'. Q4_0: the artifact's referenced file (unsloth Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q4_0.gguf, 17,379,987,872 B per HF) averages 4.55 bpw vs the row's 4.5 (negligible).
